research_mode: official ONS and Home Office Homicide Index methodology only; low-volume, snapshot, demographic and comparability gates; no parcel, exact-location, candidate or business result claimed

sources.name: Homicide Index record-level source
verified_claims: The analysis uses detailed record-level information from the Home Office Homicide Index.
limitations: National record-level homicide data do not establish a parcel-specific risk value.

sources.name: Accredited homicide statistics
verified_claims: Statistics based on the Homicide Index are accredited official statistics independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation.
limitations: Accreditation does not eliminate sampling-free administrative-data revision or classification limitations.

sources.name: Detail and publication-delay tradeoff
verified_claims: The Homicide Index provides more detail than the main police-recorded crime collection but takes longer to collect and analyse.
limitations: Detailed Homicide Index values should not be substituted for the most recent headline police count without date alignment.

sources.name: Homicide victim count
verified_claims: There were 522 homicide victims recorded in the year ending March 2025, 8% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: The annual victim count is a national statistic and not a local probability.

sources.name: Homicide population rate
verified_claims: The homicide rate was 8.6 victims per million population in the year ending March 2025, the lowest since 1977.
limitations: A national population rate must not be assigned to an individual property or neighbourhood.

sources.name: Victim sex counts
verified_claims: Male victim numbers fell to 366 while female victim numbers were 155 in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Sex-specific counts do not independently explain causal risk.

sources.name: Teenage-victim change
verified_claims: There were 34 teenage homicide victims aged 13 to 19, with sharp-instrument homicides in this group falling from 54 to 22.
limitations: Low subgroup counts are volatile and unsuitable for parcel-level inference.

sources.name: Three-year ethnicity rates
verified_claims: Over the three years to March 2025, the homicide rate for the Black ethnic group was 36.8 per million compared with 7.7 for the White ethnic group.
limitations: Age, region, socioeconomic conditions and other confounders mean the rates must not be treated as independent causal effects.

sources.name: Knife homicide change
verified_claims: Knife or sharp-instrument homicide victims fell by 21% to 205 in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Weapon-method counts do not identify exact incident locations or current parcel conditions.

sources.name: Incident and victim distinction
verified_claims: There were 508 separate homicide incidents and 522 victims in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Victim counts and incident counts are different measures and must not be combined as one total.

sources.name: Incident-change significance
verified_claims: The change in the number of homicide incidents from the previous year was not statistically significant.
limitations: A numerical decrease must not be labelled a confirmed trend without the significance result.

sources.name: Low-volume volatility
verified_claims: Homicide is a relatively low-volume offence and annual subgroup figures can fluctuate.
limitations: Small-number percentage changes can be unstable and unsuitable for fine-grained scoring.

sources.name: Multiple-victim incident effect
verified_claims: Single incidents involving multiple victims can materially affect annual homicide trends.
limitations: Annual victim movements must not be assumed to reflect broad geographic change.

sources.name: Year-of-recording convention
verified_claims: Homicide Index data are allocated to the year when the offence was recorded, not necessarily when it occurred or was heard in court.
limitations: Recorded-year data must not be interpreted as exact incident-year data in every case.

sources.name: Continuously updated index snapshot
verified_claims: The Homicide Index is updated as investigations and court cases progress, then frozen for a publication analysis snapshot.
limitations: Later extracts can revise case attributes and must be versioned by extraction date.

sources.name: Demographic non-causality warning
verified_claims: Sex, age and ethnicity are not necessarily independently related to homicide because other factors also matter.
limitations: Demographic associations must not be converted into individual or parcel risk labels.

sources.name: Homicide suspect definition
verified_claims: A Homicide Index suspect is a person charged with homicide or a person suspected by police who is known to have died.
limitations: Suspect status is not equivalent to conviction for every person.

sources.name: Principal and secondary suspect rule
verified_claims: Where several suspects exist, the Homicide Index identifies principal and secondary suspects using conviction, sentence or police-assessment rules.
limitations: The principal-suspect category is an analytical classification and must not replace case-level legal findings.

sources.name: International comparison boundary
verified_claims: ONS advises caution when comparing homicide rates internationally because definitions and systems differ.
limitations: Cross-country rates require harmonised definitions and periods.

sources.name: Homicide Index and police collection distinction
verified_claims: Homicide Index figures can differ from headline police-recorded homicide figures because the index incorporates more detailed information including court outcomes.
limitations: The two collections must not be joined without source and snapshot labels.
